## Video 1 — `print_per_layer`

### What is visibly observed
- **Website surface:** The video starts with D&D Beyond’s blank/loading page, navigation header, D&D Beyond loader, promotional banner, and **“Your Privacy Choices”** cookie banner. These are D&D Beyond’s own UI and are not extension work.
- **Website surface:** The character sheet for “Corvo Saggio” loads and displays the normal statistics, abilities, actions, and other character information.
- **Extension work:** Near the end, the sheet is enhanced with:
  - a dark floating **Beyond Print** control panel on the left;
  - a separate dark **Layer Management** panel on the right;
  - gold/red borders and handles around sheet sections;
  - a centered hint reading **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”**
- The Layer Management panel visibly contains **SECTIONS (22)** and **SHAPES (1)** groups, with section names and shape thumbnails/rows. Small control icons are present, but no print, visibility, lock, or edit control is visibly operated.
- The video ends while the enhanced layout is merely displayed. No layer is toggled, locked, unlocked, dragged, reordered, printed, or visibly re-enabled.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence
- **Layer Management panel lists layer rows with Print/Visibility/Edit controls — VISIBLE in part.** Section rows, a shape row, and compact control icons are visible, although their functions are not demonstrated.
- **Toggling Print Visibility disables the layer on print (data + button + CSS) — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Toggle back re-enables print visibility and clears the print-disabled rule — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Toggling layer Visibility hides and restores the layer DOM container — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Locking/unlocking a shape layer flips the Edit control and applies locked styling — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Section list mirrors front-to-back order and syncs print z-index (top = highest) — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Print CSS enforces layer priority (sections 1000 vs shape layers 2000) — NOT-VISIBLE.** No print preview, print operation, or resulting CSS is shown.

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance
- **Distinguishability:** Good. The extension’s dark panels, gold hairlines, red/gold section framing, and hint card are visibly unlike the base D&D Beyond sheet.
- **Basic affordances observed working:**
  - The extension overlay/panels load and appear over the sheet.
  - The Layer Management panel opens with separate section and shape groupings.
  - The sheet’s enhanced section outlines/handles are rendered.
  - The first-run/default-layout hint is displayed.
- **Missing or rough affordances:**
  - No Print, Visibility, Edit, lock, or unlock control is visibly exercised.
  - No print state or print preview is shown.
  - No visibility hide/restore transition is shown.
  - No locked styling or Edit-state transition is shown.
  - No reordering, z-index, or front-to-back synchronization is shown.
  - No toast, success confirmation, error state, or meaningful disabled state is shown for these operations.
  - The enhancement appears abruptly near the end; no clear extension-specific loading or activation transition is visible.
  - The hint card remains open while the user is expected to operate the panels, which slightly obscures the top of the enhanced sheet.

---

## Video 2 — `section_print_order`

### What is visibly observed
- **Website surface:** The same D&D Beyond loading sequence, promotional banner, cookie/privacy dialog, and plain character sheet are shown first. These are not extension work.
- **Extension work:** Near the end, the extension adds the dark floating control panel, the Layer Management panel, enhanced section outlines, and the default-layout hint card.
- The Layer Management panel shows **SECTIONS (22)** and **SHAPES (1)**. Section rows are listed in a grid-like arrangement, and shape thumbnails appear below.
- The panel is displayed, but no section card is visibly dragged. The list does not visibly change order, and no DOM-order or print-z-index result is shown before the video ends.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence
- **Top-of-list card carries the highest print z (front-to-back mirror) — NOT-VISIBLE.** No print z-index value or resulting print order is exposed on camera.
- **Dragging the top card to the bottom lowers its print z and reorders the DOM — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- **Dragging the last card back to the top gives it the highest print z — NOT-VISIBLE.**
- The Layer Management panel and its section rows are visible, but the drag behavior that constitutes this suite’s evidence is not witnessed.

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance
- **Distinguishability:** Good. The extension’s dark codex-like controls and decorative gold/red sheet treatment are clearly separate from D&D Beyond’s own red-and-white presentation.
- **Basic affordances observed working:**
  - Extension panels and section outlines render successfully.
  - The section and shape inventories populate.
  - The default-template hint appears.
- **Missing or rough affordances:**
  - No drag-and-drop affordance is demonstrated.
  - No reorder feedback, insertion position, animation, or resulting list order is shown.
  - No confirmation that the top item receives the highest print priority is shown.
  - No DOM reorder or print-layer precedence is visible.
  - No success toast, error state, invalid-drop state, or disabled drag state is shown.
  - The suite-specific interaction is not sampled before the video ends, leaving the feature largely unverified on camera.

Both recordings show the extension and its UI clearly, but neither records the asserted interactions needed to certify the print-per-layer or section-print-order behavior.
